paragraphs: EffiGov builds AI phone agents for local government. Every department gets its own agent, trained on that department's own services, hours, and escalation rules. The buyers are cities, counties, and special districts.

Agents hand a call to each other, or to a person, with the conversation carried forward. Before a resident is connected to staff, the agent briefs that staff member out loud. The agents plug into municipal systems of record, so a call resolves against live data instead of a script. A reported problem becomes a tracked record, with a reference number read back on the call. No phone system is replaced: a government forwards its existing lines to a number EffiGov manages.

The company says it is live in production across four states. Its homepage counts more than 12,000 calls in a single month, with 72 percent handled without staff. EffiGov states that a SOC 2 Type II audit is in progress. It claims zero data retention with its AI model provider and US-based data. The site says the company is backed by Y Combinator.

quote.text: Government isn’t one department, so its AI shouldn’t be one bot.
